quoted_clause: 70B dense FP16 | 140 GB | — | — | 1 GPU | 1 (140 GB weights across the 8-GPU pool, ~17.5 GB/GPU under TP
observed: The table cell says GPUs per instance is 1 for a 140 GB FP16 70B model, but the parenthetical says the 140 GB weights are spread across the 8-GPU pool at ~17.5 GB/GPU.
evidence: An H100 has 80 GB HBM; 140 GB cannot reside on one GPU. 140/8 = 17.5 GB/GPU, matching the parenthetical. The 70B MoE FP16 row has the same 140 GB / 1 GPU pattern.
root_cause: The cell likely records '1 instance' in the 'GPUs per instance' column, or the canonical 8-GPU placement was not transcribed.
correction: Set GPUs per instance to 8 for the canonical 70B dense FP16 and 70B MoE FP16 rows, or explicitly state the minimum 2-GPU placement and the canonical 8-GPU placement used for the 436 GB KV budget.
acceptance_test: Every row's weights plus per-instance KV fit within the stated per-GPU HBM, and the table matches the 8xH100 canonical host used in Ch 17.

page_hint: Ch 18, §18.3.3, Placement assumption, per-tier C and N
quoted_clause: Under dedicated placement each tier gets its own group: 8-bit C = ⌊506/24.89⌋ = 20 → 13 + 4 + 3 = 20 hosts / 32 with policy.
observed: The dedicated-placement C = 20 assumes one 70 GB 8-bit weight set resident in the 8-GPU pool, but Table 18-1 says 8-bit needs 2 GPUs per instance and 4 instances if that model alone occupies the pool.
evidence: Four 2-GPU 8-bit instances use 4 × 70 = 280 GB weights, leaving 640 − 280 − 64 = 296 GB KV and C = ⌊296/24.89⌋ = 11. One 2-GPU instance has 160 − 70 = 90 GB KV and C = 3. C = 20 comes from 640 − 70 − 64 = 506 GB, i.e. one 8-bit model using the whole 8-GPU pool, which is not the stated 2-GPU instance placement.
root_cause: The dedicated placement is not specified: one 8-bit model per 8-GPU host versus four 2-GPU instances per host.
correction: State the dedicated placement explicitly. If one 8-bit model per host uses the 8-GPU pool, change the table or add a placement note and keep C = 20. If four 2-GPU instances are used, recompute C ≈ 11 and the 13 + 4 + 3 / 32 host counts.
acceptance_test: The C derivation matches the GPUs-per-instance and instance-count assumptions, and the policy host count is derived per tier from the same C.

page_hint: Ch 17, §17.4, subsystem time table, W_e2e row
quoted_clause: ≈ 10 s planning round (Ch 4: retrieval ~0.12 s + prefill 1.08 s + decode 7.5 s, rounded)
observed: The listed components sum to 8.7 s, not ≈10 s.
evidence: 0.12 + 1.08 + 7.5 = 8.7 s. Rounding 8.7 s gives 9 s, not 10 s, unless an additional ~1.3 s component is present.
root_cause: Either the W_e2e value is over-rounded or a queue/orchestration/planning component is omitted from the parenthetical decomposition.
correction: Change the value to ≈9 s, or add the missing ~1.3 s component (for example queueing or orchestration) and label it explicitly.
acceptance_test: The named components sum to the printed W_e2e value within the stated rounding tolerance.

page_hint: Ch 17, §17.4, Effect on the headline counts
quoted_clause: only cases (ii)/(iii) bind, and there the policy screens already reported in Table 17-1 carry the extra hosts (29 under case (i), 32 under case (iii), 34 under case (ii)).
observed: The KV policy total is 32. Case (i) is 29, below 32; case (iii) is 32, equal to 32; only case (ii) is 34, above 32.
evidence: Table 17-1 and the surrounding text give policy prefill screens of 29 (case i), 32 (case iii), and 34 (case ii), versus KV-only policy total 32.
root_cause: The summary sentence conflates 'binds or ties' with 'carries extra hosts' and includes case (i) in the extra-hosts list.
correction: Rewrite as: 'only case (ii) exceeds the KV policy screen (34 vs 32); case (iii) ties it (32); case (i) is below it (29).'
acceptance_test: The sentence matches max(KV screen, prefill screen) for each FLOP-counting case.

quoted_clause: Sizing at the 25 ms budget is a tighter internal target than the 40 ms SLO pole, so name the sizing pole once and state it once: sizing at the SLO pole gives ~31 hosts
observed: The chapter's headline 31 working hosts is derived from the 25 ms budget under the 70% × 95% policy. The 40 ms SLO pole gives ~31 hosts only as a full-utilization KV screen, not as the policy working count.
evidence: At 40 ms/token, W ≈ 13.1 s, in-flight ≈ 523, full-utilization hosts ≈ ⌈523/17⌉ = 31. Under the policy, ⌈523/(17 × 0.70 × 0.95)⌉ = ⌈523/11.305⌉ = 47 working hosts, 48 with N−1.
root_cause: The coincidental equality of the 25 ms policy working count (31) and the 40 ms full-utilization count (31) is not disambiguated.
correction: State explicitly which W and which derate produce the quoted 31: 'The headline 31 working hosts uses the 25 ms budget under u × ρ; the 40 ms SLO pole gives ~31 hosts at full utilization, or ~47 working hosts under u × ρ.'
acceptance_test: A reader cannot infer that the 40 ms SLO pole is the sizing pole or that the quoted 31 is a policy count.

page_hint: Ch 17, §17.8, Initial sizing analysis, prefix-reuse W(3)
quoted_clause: under 100% prefix reuse only the final call's new context is prefilled — 11,600 tokens, i.e. 2,400 new tokens (3 × 800 of retrieved context) once the 9,200-token prefix is served from cache; the 195 generated γ tokens are not prefilled — giving W(3) ≈ 14.14 s
observed: 11,600 tokens includes the initial 9,200-token prefix. If that 9,200-token prefix were served from cache and not prefilled, the prefill sum would be 2,400 tokens, not 11,600, and W(3) would not be 14.14 s.
root_cause: The prose describes the 11,600-token prefill sum as 'only the final call's new context' while the arithmetic includes the initial 9,200-token prefill.
correction: Rewrite as: 'under 100% prefix reuse the initial 9,200 tokens are prefilled once and each turn's new 800 tokens are prefilled when appended (total 11,600); the grown prefix and the 195 γ tokens are not re-prefilled.'
acceptance_test: The prose matches the W_reuse formula and the 14.14 s value.

page_hint: Ch 19, §19.8, Unconditional fallback-inclusive ledger and note
quoted_clause: Completed T = 1 (68%) | 220 ms | 19,265 | 365 | 19,630 | ≈26.4 GB ... The T = 1 and fallback rows quote the last retained context without a separate terminal answer on top
observed: The completed T = 1 row has a terminal 300-token answer, but its peak KV is printed as ≈26.4 GB, which corresponds to 10,065 tokens before the final answer. Table 19-1 and §4 use the incl.-output peak, 10,365 tokens ≈ 27.2 GB. The completed T = 2 row has the same issue: ≈28.6 GB corresponds to 10,930 tokens, while Table 19-1 prints ≈29.4 GB for 11,230 tokens.
evidence: 10,065 × 2.62144 MB ≈ 26.38 GB; 10,365 × 2.62144 MB ≈ 27.17 GB. 10,930 × 2.62144 MB ≈ 28.65 GB; 11,230 × 2.62144 MB ≈ 29.44 GB. §4 states peak residency follows the incl.-output convention for T = 3 (12,095 → 31.7 GB).
root_cause: The ledger mixes two peak-KV conventions: pre-synthesis retained context for T = 1/T = 2/fallback and incl.-output retained context for completed T = 3.
correction: Use one convention for all completed rows. If peak means end-of-decode, print 27.2 GB for T = 1 and 29.4 GB for T = 2. If peak means pre-synthesis, apply that to T = 3 as well and reconcile with Table 19-1 and Ch 17.
acceptance_test: The ledger's peak KV column matches the §4 incl.-output convention and Table 19-1 for every completed row, or the alternative convention is stated and applied consistently.

quoted_clause: 290 GB < the canonical 436 GB KV budget, so the FP16 tier cannot co-reside at the canonical profile.
observed: The same paragraph lists one 70B dense FP16 model among the co-resident weights and then computes a shared pool C = 9 for canonical requests.
evidence: The list includes 'One 70B dense FP16 (140 GB)'. The shared pool has 640 − 350 − 64 = 226 GB KV and C = ⌊226/24.89⌋ = 9.
root_cause: The sentence conflates the FP16 tier's standalone 436 GB KV budget with the shared co-resident pool's reduced KV budget.
correction: Rewrite as: 'the FP16 tier cannot retain its standalone 436 GB KV budget while co-resident; the shared pool supports C = 9 canonical requests.'
acceptance_test: The text no longer contradicts the co-resident list or the C = 9 calculation.

page_hint: Ch 17, Table 17-1 paragraph, recomputed canonical peak screens

page_hint: Ch 17, §17.4, decode-leg feasibility at canonical peak load
quoted_clause: 12,000 × (140/17 + 24.1) GB/token ≈ 388 TB/s — weights per token at B = 17 plus the ≈24.1 GB KV re-read each output token costs
observed: 24.1 GB is the 9,200-token initial residency, but the canonical per-request max KV used for B = 17 is 9,500 tokens ≈ 24.9 GB.
evidence: 9,500 × 2.62144 MB ≈ 24.9037 GB. Using 24.9037 GB gives 12,000 × (140/17 + 24.9037) ≈ 397.6 TB/s, not 388 TB/s. The conclusion (≈14× HBM) is unchanged, but the number is inconsistent with the 9.5K max-context assumption.
root_cause: Mixed use of the 9.2K initial residency and the 9.5K max per-request KV.
correction: Use 24.9 GB and recompute ≈398 TB/s, or explicitly state that 24.1 GB is an initial-input-only approximation and show the resulting bound.
acceptance_test: The per-token KV term matches the per-request KV length used for B = 17.

quoted_clause: 70B dense 8-bit on 2×H100 (or 1×H100 with FP8 KV + offload, shown feasible)
observed: The chunk does not show 1×H100 with FP8 KV + offload to be feasible for the canonical 9,500-token request; §18.3.1 says 1×H100 8-bit has only ~10 GB KV headroom and zero concurrent canonical requests.

quoted_clause: Consolidate when: workload profile overlap ≥70%, latency tolerance ≥300 ms, and cost differential >30%.

quoted_clause: against 21/31 single-model under the canonical C = 17 — 31 (no spare) / 32 (with the N−1 spare, the Ch 17 provisioned fleet)

quoted_clause: they drive β, the p50/p90/p95 headline (220 / 440 / 660 ms), the W tool leg, and the §8 SLA scoping

quoted_clause: 12,095 tokens at T = 3 (Table 19-1), whereas Σ per-call input across the task is 23,927 tokens/request — §8 ledger — and that is the token count the cost model uses

quoted_clause: one host here serves the model on one GPU, so the per-host rate is the per-GPU rate above
observed: The same paragraph says a 7B model can be data-parallel replicated ×8 on the host. If 8 GPUs serve, the per-host rate is 8× the per-GPU rate, not the per-GPU rate.

correction: State the placement: if one GPU per host is used, keep the per-host rate equal to the per-GPU rate; if 8 data-parallel instances are used, multiply the per-GPU rate by 8 and recompute host count.
